set.approach: Reach the base of Hinterland Buttress from the main gully, then use the cut-across at the bottom of the buttress to get into the right-hand gully. The route is about halfway up Hinterland Corridor on the right edge of the buttress that divides the right and left gullies, and starts from a big ledge at its base.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the anchor at the top.

set.approach: Follow the approach to the toe of Hinterland Buttress but do not stop there; keep going up Echo Gully, passing the buttress, to the clean tower on the upper right (north) side of the gully with the keyhole through its top. Leave packs in the shady alcove at the foot of Short Round and start from just outside it.

review.notes: Key Hole Tower page and route page. No descent stated.

set.approach: Lower Dinosaur Rock is reached by a good trail from the edge of Campsite 2. Enter the hidden corridor from the east; the south side climbs are on your left. The route is in the center of the corridor, just left of T-Rex.

From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Lime-Aid is south of Table Top Rock and a little southwest of Shark Fin; it can be easier to hike straight uphill from the west end of Pioneer Lane. The route starts from a downed log on the left side of the west face.

From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Lime-Aid is south of Table Top Rock and a little southwest of Shark Fin; it can be easier to hike straight uphill from the west end of Pioneer Lane. The route goes straight up the center of the west face.

Park at Lake George and walk around the right side of the lake, then follow the dry creek or the trail on the north side of Crystal Creek. The wall sits just above a huge boulder in the creek that you can see from below; the other way in is to take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the lake, and descend to the wall. This is the center route on the wall.

Park at Lake George and walk around the right side of the lake, then follow the dry creek or the trail on the north side of Crystal Creek. The wall sits just above a huge boulder in the creek that you can see from below; the other way in is to take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the lake, and descend to the wall. This is the route farthest to the right.

Park at Lake George and walk around the right side of the lake, then follow the dry creek or the trail on the north side of Crystal Creek. The wall sits just above a huge boulder in the creek that you can see from below; the other way in is to take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the lake, and descend to the wall. This is the farthest left (downhill) route on the wall.
Take the good trail from the edge of Campsite 2 to Lower Dinosaur Rock, then skirt along its east side and head west to the foot of the south face. The route starts just right of Better than Dip.

Start from the Pine Creek pack station and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. Miner Wall is a bright green and gray face below and left of the main Brownstone Buttress, easy to see from the trail but with a bit more talus hopping to reach, and a splitter crack runs up its middle. The route is left of the Brownstone crack.

Start from the Pine Creek pack station and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. Miner Wall is a bright green and gray face below and left of the main Brownstone Buttress, easy to see from the trail but with a bit more talus hopping to reach, and a splitter crack runs up its middle. The route is the first one right of the central crack; start just right of a low roof and trend left up the slab.

Start from the Pine Creek pack station and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. Miner Wall is a bright green and gray face below and left of the main Brownstone Buttress, easy to see from the trail but with a bit more talus hopping to reach, and a splitter crack runs up its middle. The route is the second one to the right of the Brownstone crack.
Hike up to Church Domes; Miracle Revival Dome is the quickest of them to reach. Its west face holds the climbing, and this line sits immediately left of Forgive Me Father.

From the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles northern parking area, a network of trails leads to Motherlode Rock; the east face can also be reached from The Amphitheatre. The route is a direct start to Shantytown Swing from the ground and joins it at the top of the ramp.
Start at the northern parking area; the trail runs under the Incinerator Wall and ends at the narrow, shaded north face. The route is a link-up that starts up Short Fuse and finishes on Boom Sauce.

From the northern parking area follow the trail that passes beneath the Incinerator Wall, then cut right up the steep rocky gully below the left side of the west face. The route is the second one right of Good Day for a Hangin', beside a pine tree.

Follow the John Muir Trail (the Cathedral Lakes trail) from Tuolumne Meadows; the buttress toe is a very short distance from the trail. After Party begins at the top of Garden Party, so climb that route first.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from the belay anchors, which have rappel rings.

review.notes: Area page for approach; route page for the start and the rappels.

set.approach: Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Close to where it tops out, bear onto the right fork and cross the talus field to the foot of the north face. The route is the furthest bolted line on the right, just right of Dominatrix, and starts in a prominent undercling right off the ground.

Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Bear onto the right fork where it tops out and cross the talus to the main north face; this route is on a lower wall a short way down the talus from it. It climbs the left side of a clean arete just right of Special Fun.

Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Close to where it tops out, bear onto the right fork and cross the talus field to the foot of the north face. The route is on the technical face left of Dominatrix.

Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Close to where it tops out, bear onto the right fork and cross the talus field to the foot of the north face. The route is left of the Mongoloid arete, on the east-facing part of the north wall.

Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Close to where it tops out, bear onto the right fork and cross the talus field to the foot of the north face. The route takes the far left, slabby arete of the face.

Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Bear onto the right fork where it tops out and cross the talus to the main north face; this route is on a separate cliff a short way down the talus to the west. Of the two bolted lines there, take the left one, up the middle of the face.

Park where forest roads 2N13 and 2N13D meet and use the climbers trail that climbs the ramp over the gully. The North Side Lower Tier is the first side you see from the road, with a trail leading straight to it. The route is on the slab left of a slanting crack.

Park where forest roads 2N13 and 2N13D meet and use the climbers trail that climbs the ramp over the gully. The North Side Lower Tier is the first side you see from the road, with a trail leading straight to it. The route is the farthest right slab on the north side, and it shares a top-out with Southwest of Spy.
